windows.text:
Severe stress/adrenal fatigue/poor sleep (Phase 1): This can cause a lack of mucus to line the stomach, which in turn causes burning, difficulty absorbing nutrients, and so forth. And every other gut issue can also be partly related to this. My mindset page and loveyhuasca protocol can help a lot with this, as well as my deep sleep tips.
Sitting, or lack of exercise and stretching (Phase 5): humans were not designed to be sedentary. Our biology slows down and cramps up when we are. Walk, do yoga, do shaking qi-gong, do bodyweight strength training.
This woman healed her gut with 3 fun movements:
Actually, yoga specifically, and especially Iyengar yoga, which is the most technically anatomical scientific yoga, would be more useful than general exercise:
Poor diet now (Phase 2): industrial and processed foods, especially oils, are often empty calories full of countless toxins and oxidation byproducts. Toxins are sequestered in fat cells to prevent them from damaging organs, but this toxic fat (especially visceral fat) becomes a chronic health issue even as it protects us from immediately dying from the sequestered toxins.
Parasites, H. pylori, mold, metals (Phases 3 and 6): We are often addicted to junk food due to a vicious cycle in which the junk feeds parasitic organisms and bad bacteria, yeast, etc, which then send signals to our brain to consume more junk. Thus, we have to target the problem from various angles — cleansing out pathogens, repopulating good bacteria, addressing vitamin (especially thiamine), mineral, and enzyme deficiencies, and changing what we eat. I wrote about my detox protocol (which includes the gut) here. For H. Pylori specifically: if you get heartburn when your stomach is empty only, that's usually H. Pylori, and it's easily treated with berberine.

windows.label: Human Written
windows.text:
Years of accumulated shit in your guts (closest: Phase 4): This part isn't in the gut healing books I read, but even if you fix all of what's going into you now, if you're already full and clogged with all of what went in before, that's gonna be little help. My friend Pooyan got incredibly healthier and happier after getting enough colon hydrotherapy to flush that stuff out, combined with then also doing intense stretches like hanging from one arm, until finally, the most crusted up shit exploded in him which was very painful for a day.
This is likely caused by diverticulosis, a disease that causes herniated pockets to form in the intestines which aren't supported by smooth muscle. There's no known cure for this disease, except possibly glutamine, based one one incompleted clinical trial, which found 2 of 9 women had incredible reductions in diverticula. Glutamine an amino acid that's the fuel for small intestinal cells, so this makes some sense. 10% of people get side effects from it (including constipation). Butyrate is the fuel for the colon cells. I would also suggest diosmin for improving blood vessel integrity.
However, while we don't know if Pooyan has diverticulosis, what we now do know is that his peak health disappeared 3 days later after eating some bread with A1 dairy.
CAUTION: If you have severe diverticulosis, especially diverticulitis (once the fecal impaction causes intestinal infection & inflammation), you might be at high risk for intestinal wall rupture, and even rejected by the more reputable colonic irrigation clinics. Make sure you get cleared by a gastroenterologist first.

windows.label: Human Written
windows.text:
SIBO (Phases 3 and 5): Small intestinal bacterial overgrowth is a huge issue underlying a wide range of illnesses. One of the most effective cures for many people is SIBO Yogurt. I also sell these SIBO yogurt bacteria (along with other helpful herbal juices and minerals) in liquid form for vegans.
Plant foods (Phases 2 and 5): The carnivore diet is trending, as many people (especially with leaky gut or lack of oxalate-processing bacteria) are noticing they cannot handle fiber, oxalates, and phytates in plants. It's certainly a diet worth trying, but it can lead to deficiencies over time, especially with regard vitamins C, E, fiber, magnesium, potassium, calcium, iodine and other trace minerals, and bacteria needed to process plant foods (which already are likely missing in people who need this diet), thus making the carnivore diet sort of hard to get off.
For the most research-backed recommendations you can check this HRP deep research report. Glutamine seems worth checking into, but plant intolerance is a symptom of a variety of underlying diseases that all have different treatments.
IBS (Phase 4): While there are many causes and types of irritable bowel syndrome, psychedelics are one promising new avenue of treatment. However, it's always best to find the root cause of the problem, which requires investigation. A functional medicine gastroenterologist might help.
Low stomach acid, enzymes, and thick bile (Phase 1): which in turn are often due to poor diet, stress, infections. T.C. Hale has a lot of videos on healing digestion issues, which in his experience as a health coach, are often due to these root causes. He's a bit controversial on some points such as his urine pH testing for anabolic/catabolic state freezes, but he does have some good suggestions he explains in his book.

windows.label: Human Written
windows.text:
Leaky gut (Phase 5): a widespread inflammatory condition often intersecting with other categories of illness such as Crohn's Disease or IBS, plant food intolerance, and what many alternative health practitioners consider as a root cause of most diseases. It's associated with increased zonulin levels clinically. Zonulin is the molecule released to signal your intestinal tight jungtions to open. Too much opening time leads to allowing stuff to leak out into your blood stream which then burdens your immune system and detoxification systems. Game-changing treatments:
Liposomal first-milking colostrum (esp. fermented per Matt Nedin's protocol with bifidobacterium, or SIBO yogurt bacteria). Matt from Endsickness.org finds that this helps especially to mop up mycotoxins in the gut. Activated charcoal can also be helpful, altho don't take that with things you want to actually absorb.
Fermented veggie juices of turmeric, red cabbage, celery, beet greens (not just beet root).
Zinc carnosine, the form of zinc which stays in your intestinal gaps.
